literal_math_description: Build a finite connected two-layer Hopf-torus carrier fixture from two fixed-theta torus layers plus interlayer faces, and compare topology readouts across two independent tools.
operation_sequence: sample two fixed-theta Hopf tori in S3
construct periodic torus layer cells or triangulations
add interlayer faces in both torus coordinate directions
compute finite topology readouts using TopoNetX and GUDHI
compute S3 norm and interlayer embedding-distance diagnostics
run disjoint-layer, single-direction-connection, duplicate-theta, collapsed/no-face graveyards
carrier_topology: finite two-layer Hopf-torus carrier fixture with interlayer faces over corresponding periodic grid coordinates; no full geometric constraint manifold
observable: cell/simplex counts, incidence shapes, Hodge-Laplacian zero-mode proxies, Betti readouts, S3 norm error, and interlayer S3 distance diagnostics
pass_fail_predicate: connected two-layer fixtures have one component readout, expected loop readouts for the finite fixture, expected counts, unit S3 embeddings, and separated theta layers; adjacent controls collapse or expose missing connection/layer geometry
graveyards: single interlayer direction keeps extra loop readouts
duplicated theta values remove interlayer embedding separation
collapsed point is not a connected layer carrier
rank-2 faces removed do not have torus layer topology
baselines: TopoNetX two disjoint Hopf-torus layer incidence fixture
GUDHI Hopf torus fiber/base homology fixture
three-formulation Hopf phase-generator density transport packet
SymPy Hopf connection curvature and horizontal-lift fixtures
alternative_formulations: density-object evolution over connected carrier coordinates
nested horizontal-lift ODE integration over multiple theta layers
claim_ceiling: two-tool finite topology baseline packet only; no physical inner/outer loop independence, no full S3 bundle, no flux, no QIT, GStack, axis, bridge, nonclassical, target-system, or full geometric-constraint-manifold admission
blocked_until: explicit connection or transport law over the connected carrier exists
declared physical or geometric observables are fixed before the run
operator/density evolution over connected carrier coordinates exists
physical-evolution or carrier-topology graveyards reproduce compatible collapse behavior
